Thresholds without an AWS-published value are marked `workload-specific` at severity INFO.\\n\\n| check-id | pillar | severity | detection-rule | remediation | AWS-doc-citation |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| LLM-AC-001 | Security/Responsible-AI | CRITICAL | The AgentCore runtime execution role\\'s identity policies, evaluated statically (`iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy` is never called; label \"evaluated from policy documents, not simulated\"), show a required action is denied \u2014 e.g. `bedrock:InvokeModel` / `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream`, `s3:GetObject` for artifacts/KB sources, `logs:CreateLogStream`/`logs:PutLogEvents`, or the `bedrock:` actions behind the `bedrock-agent-runtime` operations it calls (for example `bedrock:Retrieve`, `bedrock:InvokeAgent`). The agent cannot invoke models or read its dependencies. | Grant the runtime role least-privilege permissions for every action it exercises (model invoke on the specific model/inference-profile ARNs, S3 read on the source bucket, CloudWatch Logs write, gateway target actions); re-read the policies until every required action is allowed. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-permissions.html |\\n| LLM-AC-002 | Security/Responsible-AI | HIGH | An Organizations SCP applies an explicit `Deny` to actions AgentCore needs (`bedrock:*`, `bedrock-agentcore:*`, or specific invoke/gateway actions) for the account/OU, so an otherwise-correct runtime role is still blocked. Detect by reading effective SCPs (`organizations:ListPoliciesForTarget` / `DescribePolicy`) and correlating with the denied action from the policy read. | Amend the SCP (or move the account to an OU) so the required AgentCore actions are not explicitly denied; an explicit SCP deny overrides any identity-based allow. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html |\\n| LLM-AC-003 | Reliability | HIGH | `ec2:DescribeVpcEndpoints` shows an endpoint missing for a VPC-deployed runtime in subnets without internet access. AWS documents `com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.dkr`, `com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.api`, the S3 gateway endpoint `com.amazonaws.<region>.s3` and `com.amazonaws.<region>.logs` as required; the agent also needs an endpoint for each AWS service its own code calls (for example `bedrock-runtime` for model calls, `bedrock-agent-runtime` for knowledge base retrieval). Traffic with no private path fails in no-egress subnets. | Create the missing endpoints (interface endpoints for ECR, Logs and the services the code calls; the S3 gateway endpoint, which AWS recommends even with a NAT gateway) with security groups allowing HTTPS from the agent subnets; verify DNS resolution and a test invocation. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/agentcore-vpc.html |\\n| LLM-AC-004 | Reliability | HIGH | The AgentCore gateway is not configured, or a gateway target is misconfigured \u2014 no gateway associated with the agent, a target endpoint/credential/schema invalid, or the target health check failing. Tool/API calls routed through the gateway cannot resolve. | Configure the gateway and each target with a valid endpoint, credential provider, and schema; validate target connectivity and correct any failing target before production use. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-building-adding-targets.html |\\n| LLM-AC-008 | Security/Responsible-AI | MEDIUM | Gateway authentication uses tokens/credentials with no configured expiration or rotation \u2014 long-lived static credentials for gateway targets, no rotation schedule. Credential compromise has an unbounded window. | Configure short-lived tokens with automatic expiration and a rotation schedule (or an OAuth/credential provider that rotates) for gateway target auth. Threshold `workload-specific`. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-outbound-auth.html |\\n| LLM-AC-009 | Operational Excellence | MEDIUM | A runtime endpoint (DEFAULT or named) serves an older agent runtime version than the one the operator expects to be live (`ListAgentRuntimeEndpoints` / `ListAgentRuntimeVersions`), so fixes in the newer version are not running. AgentCore Runtime has no built-in session replay; session recording to S3 exists for Browser sessions only (LLM-AC-013). Threshold `workload-specific`. | Instrument the agent so spans carry the session ID and appear in the Sessions view, and keep a per-session application log for debugging, regression testing and incident review. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/observability-view.html |\\n| LLM-AC-011 | Reliability/Performance | HIGH | A runtime, gateway or memory call is throttled (HTTP 429 / `ThrottlingException`) or slows under concurrency. First establish **which layer throttled**: (a) `InvokeAgentRuntime` itself returned 429 and the runtime log group has no line for that request, so the platform rejected it before the container ran: compare the aggregate rate with the account\\'s AgentCore data-plane quota (1,000 TPS shared by `InvokeAgentRuntime` and the other data-plane APIs) and, when each call or test worker uses a fresh `runtimeSessionId`, with the **new session creation rate (25 TPS per account, shared across all endpoints)**; (b) the agent code\\'s own `bedrock-runtime` `InvokeModel`/`Converse` call is throttled inside the container (the runtime log shows the model exception): that is the Bedrock model quota for that model, not an AgentCore quota; (c) gateway `tools/call`/`tools/list` above 200 TPS per gateway or per account; (d) AgentCore Memory `CreateEvent` above 5 TPS per actor per session (with conversational payloads). For (a): stagger or rate-limit callers below the quota, reuse a stable session ID per user or conversation instead of a new one per call, add client retry with exponential backoff and jitter, and request a Service Quotas increase for the adjustable quota if sustained load needs it (the quota owner is the runtime\\'s account). **1. Does the code write and read events every turn? (most common cause)**
- The code must call `CreateEvent` to save each turn and `ListEvents` (or `GetEvent`) to load the history on every invoke. Memory is not injected into the runtime automatically.
- A stable `runtimeSessionId` only routes calls to the same microVM. The runtime stores no conversation history. In-process state is lost after the 15-minute idle timeout, the 8-hour lifetime limit, or when a new microVM starts.
- If the code never writes and reads events, there is no history to lose. If you use a framework integration or hook for memory, confirm it is actually wired into the invoke path.

**2. Are `memoryId`, `actorId` and `sessionId` the same on write and read?**
- Short-term events are scoped by memory, actor and session. If any of these changes between turns, the agent reads an empty or different history. Common causes are a fresh UUID per request, a user ID that isn't stable, or two environments pointing at different memory resources.
- In a multi-agent setup, agents only share context if they use the same memory resource with consistent actor and session scoping.

**3. Is the runtime session header correct?**
- MCP runtimes use `Mcp-Session-Id`. HTTP, A2A and AG-UI runtimes use `X-Amzn-Bedrock-AgentCore-Runtime-Session-Id`.
- A wrong or missing header means a new microVM on each call, so any in-process state is lost.

**4. Are you using branches?**
- Events written with `branch` (`name`, `rootEventId`) stay on that branch. There is no merge operation, so events written to one branch after the fork don't show up in another.
- If the history looks incomplete after an edit or retry, check whether you're reading the right branch.

**5. Are you expecting long-term memory too soon?**
- Long-term records are extracted asynchronously by the memory's strategies after `CreateEvent` or `IngestData`. They aren't available immediately. Blob payloads are never extracted.
- A missing or invalid `extractionConfig` namespace variable still stores the event but may skip extraction. You'll only see this in the memory's vended logs, so enable log delivery.
- Read the records with `RetrieveMemoryRecords` or `ListMemoryRecords` under the strategy's namespace. Don't read them as short-term history.

**6. Are Memory calls failing or being throttled?**
- Check the Memory CloudWatch metrics (`CreateEvent` and `RetrieveMemoryRecords` `Invocations`, `Latency`, `Errors`) and the runtime logs for swallowed exceptions.
- `CreateEvent` is limited to 5 TPS per actor per session, so throttled writes can silently drop turns if the code doesn't handle the error.
- Check the runtime execution role for permissions on the Memory actions. For cross-account memory, the caller's identity policy and the memory's resource policy must each allow every action (`CreateEvent`, `ListEvents` and so on).

**7. Is it the Bedrock Agents Classic memory feature instead?**
- If this is a legacy Bedrock Agent, check `memoryConfiguration` on the agent and the session TTL. Memory there is tied to a stable `memoryId` and session lifetime.
